title: Check your understanding: Authentication and Credentials

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of authentication and credentials?
options: Credential helpers or SSH agents can reduce repeated authentication, but tokens and private keys must remain outside the repository. Inspect credential configuration without printing secret values.
Git automatically backs up every file, including ignored and untracked files, to a remote.
The operation grants every contributor write access to the hosted repository.
questions.answer_key: Credential helpers or SSH agents can reduce repeated authentication, but tokens and private keys must remain outside the repository. Inspect credential configuration without printing secret values.
questions.explanation: Credential helpers or SSH agents can reduce repeated authentication, but tokens and private keys must remain outside the repository. Inspect credential configuration without printing secret values.

questions.prompt: Which command is the most direct starting point for this lesson’s example?
questions.explanation: Use `git config --show-origin --get credential.helper` as the first inspection/action in the example, and then verify the result with the companion checks in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest general practice when working with authentication and credentials?
options: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
Run the most destructive option first; the reflog guarantees every file can always be recovered.
Assume the local command also changed the remote and satisfied all hosting-platform policies.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
questions.explanation: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
